page: Amazon Web Services m5n.16xlarge is a general-purpose, network-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores with hyperthreading, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 256 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

A key differentiator of this instance is its networking and memory bandwidth capabilities. It delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 75 Gbps. In memory benchmarks, the instance demonstrates strong performance in large-block uncached operations, reaching 213.54 GB/sec for read-only and 93.42 GB/sec for write operations, placing it in the top 25% of tested hardware. Small-block cached memory reads average 3013.4 GB/sec.

While multi-core and parallel processing benchmarks show average performance, single-core capabilities represent a notable tradeoff. The Intel Xeon processor scores in the bottom 25% for single-core stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks are also weak. However, multi-threaded operations, such as Passmark CPU and multi-core Geekbench, perform in the middle tier, making the instance better suited for parallelized workloads rather than single-threaded execution.

Given its high network throughput and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, the m5n.16xlarge is suited for network-heavy general-purpose workloads, multi-threaded database operations, and distributed applications. Qualitative cost efficiency is driven by its high network-to-resource density, though the lack of local storage requires accounting for external storage performance. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, Redis deployments, and parallelized data processing tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services m5n.16xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance featuring 64 vCPUs and 256 GB of DDR4 RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor at 3.1 GHz. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, it lacks local storage and GPUs but provides a high baseline network bandwidth of 75 Gbps. Benchmark data reveals a clear performance tradeoff: single-core CPU execution and single-threaded compression are weak, scoring in the bottom 25%, whereas large-block memory read and write bandwidths are strong, placing in the top 25%. Multi-core processing, database operations, and web serving throughput perform at average levels. This resource profile makes the instance suitable for network-intensive, parallelized workloads such as distributed databases, Redis deployments, and static web serving, where high network throughput and balanced memory density are prioritized over raw single-threaded CPU speed.
